title: Geohash encode, decode and neighbours
summary: Turn latitude and longitude into a base32 geohash by interleaving bisection bits, decode it back to a cell, and find the 8 cells around it.
hints: Each bit halves one interval: 1 means the point is in the upper half, 0 the lower. Bits alternate longitude, latitude, longitude, ... starting with longitude, and every 5 bits become one character of the alphabet.

Track four numbers (the low and high ends of the latitude and longitude intervals) plus a flag saying which axis the next bit splits. Decode replays the same bits from the characters, most significant bit of each character first, and the final intervals are the cell.

For a neighbour, start at the decoded centre and move exactly one cell height (2 × lat_err) or width (2 × lon_err) in the direction; that point is the centre of the neighbouring cell. Wrap longitude by ±360 if it passes ±180, return None if latitude passes a pole, and encode at the same length.
